newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK interest rate rise.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK interest rate rise.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to the decision of Britain's new monetary policy committee to raise base rates by a quarter-point to 6.5 percent.

"Very much in line with expectations and clearly reflects concerns about the strength of domestic demand. I don't think the budget will convince them that demand will be constrained sufficiently. I think we'll see another rate rise in the next few months."
"Gilts haven't moved much but this should be pretty constructive for the long end of the market, raising hopes that inflation will remain subdued."

"The only reason people were saying they may not do something was that it was so soon after the last hike and they may want to wait and see what was happening in the budget. Almost everyone agrees that there is evidence the domestic economy is growing at a very rapid pace and that further hikes in interest rates will be necessary. The next meeting comes the day after the budget, that may be too soon. One thing that has come up in recent weeks is the huge weight of windfalls from building society conversions. Eddie George was talking about that the other day. I think that must be a matter of concern for the Bank."

"Today's move demonstrates the Bank of England's concern over rapid consumer spending growth and its commitment to keep inflation within it's target range in the medium term. The path of interest rates from now on depends on the structure of next month's mini-budget and also on the effects of sterling's strength on the economy. Our central view is now that we will probably see one more rate rise in this cycle, taking base rates to 6.75 which embodies the assumption that there will be a tightening of fiscal policy next month."
